package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, enabling theft of sensitive credentials.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically during package installation.
The code reads sensitive files: ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config from the user's system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of private SSH and Kubernetes credentials.

attack_chain.action: Collected credentials are exfiltrated to the attacker's server via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to stolen credentials.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config.
The package sends outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com containing file contents.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config and posts data externally
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installation of 'pymafka' for file access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, and detect any outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com. Flag any package setup.py that reads sensitive credential files and transmits their contents to external domains. Use static analysis to identify hardcoded references to these files and the suspicious domain in package source code.
